whereas a keyless replay of a captured valid frame is re-acknowledged each time and can consume the base's downlink budget unless two limits are on, the re-acknowledgement interval and the downlink budget. We state them as deployment requirement R-REACK, with the values of the replay-flood study: no re-acknowledgement of the same event sooner than the shortest legitimate retry spacing (\RsevdIntervalSeven{} s at SF7, \RsevdIntervalEight{} s at SF8, \RsevdIntervalNine{} s at SF9), and a downlink token bucket that refills at the \RsevdDutyPct\% duty cycle with a capacity of \RsevdCapacity{} s (it started at \RsevdInitial{} s in the study). With the limits off, \RsevdRate{} replays a second for \RsevdDuration{} s of one valid alert at SF7 drew \RsevdOffReacks{} re-acknowledgements and \RsevdOffAirtime{} s of airtime, the budget ran out and a genuine alert at 100 s was accepted but not acknowledged; with them on, \RsevdOnReacks{} and \RsevdOnAirtime{} s, and the genuine alert was acknowledged. The limits stop the starvation but not the waste (the replays still spent \RsevdOnShare\% of the starting budget; a stricter limit was not evaluated). The reference verifier has both limits off by default; a new reference configuration turns them on without touching any frozen file. The ns-3 gateway model does not check tags and has no such limit.
